title: Constructive Cavity Method for Ising Restricted and Deep Boltzmann Machines with Gaussian Couplings
authors: Simone Franchini, Francesco Concetti, Giampiero Bardella, Liming Pan
abstract: We apply the Constructive Cavity Method (CCM) to the dense, Ising type, restricted and deep Boltzmann machine with Gaussian couplings between adjacent layers. After identifying the core and interface contributions, CCM identifies the blanket decomposition of the cavity variables with the Aizenman--Sims--Starr random overlap structure. We apply the Random Energy Model (REM) universality ansatz to represent the cavity free energies by those of a generalized random energy model (GREM) and evaluate them recursively through Poisson point processes (PPPs). In the layer-wise gauge each layer is cut with its own cumulative fraction $|U_\ell\cap L_p|=λ_p q_\ell^{(p)}N+o(N)$, with $\mathbf 0=\mathbf q_0\le\mathbf q_1\le\cdots\le\mathbf q_r=\mathbf 1$, where $\mathbf q_\ell=(q_\ell^{(1)},\ldots,q_\ell^{(K)})$. Here $U_\ell$ is the cumulative blanket union up to blanket $\ell$. The index $p$ labels architectural layers, whereas $\ell$ labels the blankets. The dependence on the multilayer geometry is carried by the two matrices $M=2M_0Λ$ and $M_1=ΛM_0Λ$. The constructive cavity field in layer $p$ has blanket variances $Q_\ell^{(p)}-Q_{\ell-1}^{(p)}=(M(\mathbf q_\ell-\mathbf q_{\ell-1}))_p$, while the correction field has blanket variances $Q_\ell-Q_{\ell-1}=\mathbf q_\ell^\top M_1\mathbf q_\ell-\mathbf q_{\ell-1}^\top M_1\mathbf q_{\ell-1}$. The nested REM--PPP average gives the finite-level constructive cavity functional $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{RBM/DBM}}^{\mathrm{CCM}}(ζ,\mathbf q)=\log2+\sum_{p=1}^Kλ_pX_0^{(p)}-\frac12\sum_{\ell=0}^{r-1}ζ_\ell(\mathbf q_{\ell+1}^\top M_1\mathbf q_{\ell+1}-\mathbf q_\ell^\top M_1\mathbf q_\ell)$. The balanced scalar gauge is recovered by imposing $\mathbf q_\ell=q_\ell\mathbf 1$. Selecting the physical value in the non-convex multilayer regime is a separate problem.
summary: This work develops the Constructive Cavity Method (CCM) to calculate the free energy of deep Boltzmann machines. It achieves this by decomposing the system's structure into 'blankets' and using a generalized random energy model approach. The resulting functional provides a computable, finite-level description of the system's statistical mechanics.
main_problem: The paper applies the Constructive Cavity Method (CCM) to evaluate the cavity free energy functionals for dense, Ising-type Restricted and Deep Boltzmann Machines (RBM/DBM).
main_result: It derives a finite-level constructive cavity functional, $PCCM_{RBM/DBM}(\zeta, q)$, by mapping the system's structure onto a blanket decomposition related to the Aizenman–Sims–Starr Random Overlap Structure.
method: The core method is the Constructive Cavity Method (CCM), which uses a blanket decomposition framework combined with the Random Energy Model (REM) universality ansatz and evaluation via Poisson Point Processes (PPPs).
model_or_system: The model is a multilayer RBM/DBM network with Gaussian couplings, analyzed using a layer-wise gauge defined by cumulative fractions $q_\ell$. The analysis focuses on the interface-only contributions.
key_observables: The finite-level constructive cavity functional $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{RBM/DBM}}^{\mathrm{CCM}}(\zeta,\mathbf q)$, and the spectral radius $ho(K)$ used to determine stability boundaries.
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($ eta_p$), layer proportions ($\lambda_p$), and the layer-wise gauge coordinates ($\mathbf q_\ell$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the assumption of interface dominance and explicitly notes that selecting the physical value in non-convex multilayer regimes is a separate, unaddressed problem.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the CCM blanket geometry, detailing how blankets $V_\ell$ cut nodes and how edge shells $W^{(p, p+1)}_\ell$ are formed between adjacent layers.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the CCM framework for RBM/DBM, details the blanket decomposition and the construction of cavity/correction fields, derives the final constructive functional, and analyzes stability by examining the RS splitting-instability condition.
why_interesting: While primarily focused on statistical mechanics of neural networks, the rigorous mathematical machinery involving cavity methods, replica symmetry breaking, and functional evaluation shares deep theoretical parallels with analyzing complex quantum many-body systems, particularly those involving disorder or glassy dynamics.

figures.caption: Figure 1: CCM blanket geometry for a multilayer RBM/DBM. Architectural layers are indexed by p, while CCM blankets are indexed by ℓ. Each blanket Vℓis a global partition block crossing all architectural layers, and the cell Vℓ∩Lp has size λp(q(p) ℓ −q(p) ℓ−1)N + o(N).
